variants.headline: Party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: A party leader is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
A scandal about a party leader has come to light. The revelation makes political trust an immediate subject of public attention. An assessment of {target} must distinguish that known fact from unreported details about the conduct involved, its cause or any proceedings that might follow.

In our judgment, {target} does not deserve confidence in this matter. Political trust requires a demanding standard, and the scandal is an appropriate occasion for a distinctly critical assessment.

variants.headline: Leadership under an unwelcome spotlight
variants.sub: A scandal about a party leader has become public in the colony.
variants.body:
Leadership brings a claim to trust. A newly revealed scandal concerning a party leader gives that claim an uncomfortable setting in {colony}. Readers considering {target} should be able to examine responsibility without being invited to accept a more specific accusation than the report establishes.

In our judgment, {target} does not deserve confidence in this matter. Political trust requires a demanding standard, and the scandal is an appropriate occasion for a distinctly critical assessment.

variants.headline: A scandal tests political trust
variants.sub: A scandal concerning a party leader has come to light in {colony}.
variants.body:
The public record now includes a scandal about a party leader. That is serious political news; it is not permission to fill gaps with an attractive story. For {target}, the question of trust deserves attention without a fabricated account of money, private life or criminal conduct.

In our judgment, {target} does not deserve confidence in this matter. Political trust requires a demanding standard, and the scandal is an appropriate occasion for a distinctly critical assessment.
